info.title: Sphericon Collect API
info.description: Event ingestion for customer sites and apps, authenticated by a collect key.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

default.description:
The answer of every request a surface refuses or fails (RFC 7807), whatever its status: the
status is the response's and the body's `status`, and `code` tells apart the answers a client
branches on. A 429 (a rate limit, ADR 0025) and a 503 also carry `Retry-After` and, for the
rate limit, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; the body's
`retryAfter` is the wait for a client that reads only the body. Every operation declares it,
as the `default` response (ADR 0103).

post.description: Issues a start link on the workspace's default Telegram integration. It is refused with 422 when the workspace has no enabled default one.

clientEventId.description:
A client-chosen id that makes a retry safe. It is unique within the Workspace: sending
an event again with the same id changes nothing, so a client that did not see the answer
(a network error, a `503`) resends the whole batch. Generate it once per event, when the
event happens (a UUID), and reuse it on every retry. An event without one is not deduplicated.

locale.description: The browser's language, a BCP 47 tag

CollectIdentifyContext.description: The browser's own settings, sent by the tracker with an identify

phone.description:
Phone number — an alias key, stored in E.164. A number without a country code is read with
the `country` trait or the country of the contact the other keys find; one that does not
parse is refused

traits.description:
Attributes of the contact; a trait named after a core attribute (`firstName`, `timeZone`,
`country`, `locale`, `birthday`, `city`, `avatar`) writes it, null clears it, and an invalid
value of one is dropped. Any other trait is a custom field, whose type a new key's first value
sets: a boolean, a number, a date (an ISO string: `2026-01-15T10:00:00Z`,
`2026-01-15T10:00:00` or `2026-01-15`, the last two read in the Workspace time zone) or text.
Send a date without time as a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, not a JavaScript `Date`: that serializes
as UTC and lands on the previous day east of UTC

context.description:
What the browser tells of the visitor: it fills only a time zone or locale the contact has
none of

expiresAt.description: When the link lapses, 30 days after it is issued

CollectTelegramStartLink.description: A Telegram start link for a visitor: pressing Start in the bot binds the chat to the visitor, and it reaches the contact once the visitor is identified. The link works once.

visitorId.description: The tracker's id of the visitor the link is for, created when it has not been seen

CountryCode.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, upper case (`US`, `DE`)

EditorDocument.description:
The email editor's JSON document, an opaque object the server checks against the schema
`email_schema` returns. One named model, as JsonObject.

EntityId.description:
A primary key, written as a decimal string so JavaScript never rounds it. The format
makes the Go servers parse it into an int64: a malformed id is refused as a 400 before
a handler runs. The pattern says the same in the contract, so a client (or a fuzzer) can
tell a malformed id from a valid one without trying it. Eighteen digits is the most a key
reaches, so every id the schema admits fits an int64.

ImageUrl.description: The https URL of an image

JsonObject.description:
A JSON object whose members the contract leaves open: custom field values, event properties,
integration params, an audit diff. One named model, so every surface's Go code has one type for
it rather than one per field.

LocaleTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag: a language, optionally with a script and a region (`de`, `pt-BR`)

ProblemCode.description: A machine-readable reason a client branches on, beyond the HTTP status

error.description: The error that failed the request, or the panic value

stack.description: The goroutine stack of a panic; absent for an error a handler returned

requestId.description: The request id the server log carries for this request

method.description: The HTTP method of the failed request

path.description: The path of the failed request

ProblemDebug.description:
What a development server adds to a 500 so the page can show the fault; a production
Instance never sends it

code.description: Why the request was refused, when the client should act on it

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; set on a 429 so a client that only sees the body can show the wait

debug.description: Why a 500 happened, sent only by a development server (`SPHERICON_ENV=development`)

usedBy.description:
A removal refused because live work still uses the row (a 409, ADR 0049): the rows that
use it, never empty

workspaces.description:
A refused User deletion (ADR 0050): the live Workspaces the User is the only Owner of, each
handed over or deleted first; empty when the refusal is another rule's

RegionalFormat.description:
A BCP 47 tag, with its region, that a User picks for how the app shows dates, times and
numbers (`en-GB`, `de-DE`). A malformed tag is refused by the handler (422).

SoleOwnedWorkspace.description: A Workspace the User is the only Owner of, which blocks User deletion

kind.description: What kind of row it is

count.description:
How many rows the entry stands for; absent means one. An `enrollment` entry names the
Automation (id, name) and counts its active Enrollments.

UsedBy.description:
A row that uses the one a removal was refused for: what a client shows to say what to
change first

UsedByKind.description:
What kind of row a refused removal names as a user of the row (ADR 0049). One value per kind
of live user a removal can find, so a client branches on it without parsing text.

WorkspaceId.description:
A Workspace id (ADR 0043): 8 random base62 characters, assigned once at creation and the
Workspace's one public address.
